clue.text: Incomparable lady enthralling all at last

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the lady's word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a peeress is a woman holding a title in the peerage

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word all and nothing else

parts.note: last letter of all

explanation.surface: A matchless woman who keeps everyone spellbound right to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: PEERESS takes L into its middle: PEER-L-ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something peerless has no equal, so it cannot be compared with anything else.

clue.text: Adept former schoolteacher

parts.note: past means earlier or former
a master is a traditional term for a male schoolteacher

explanation.surface: Someone who used to teach school, still skilled at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adept' is the noun here, an expert, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A past master is an expert thoroughly skilled in some activity, just as an adept is.

clue.text: Burp is routine act, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters before it come out in a bad order

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Sadly, burping has become a regular part of someone's performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Eructation is the formal medical word for belching, the release of stomach gas through the mouth.

clue.text: Northern girl picked up drink

indicators.note: picked up is used as in catching a radio signal, i.e. heard rather than seen

parts.note: lassie is the Scottish and northern English word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl from the north grabs something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassi is a yoghurt-based drink from the Indian subcontinent, sweet or salty.

clue.text: Evanescence of our stellar setter

parts.note: surface reading: the passing of a brilliant crossword setter, the puzzle's dedicatee
cryptic reading: our own star, the sun, which sets; its brief vanishing is the event

explanation.surface: A tribute lamenting the loss of a brilliant crossword compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle remembers the setter Nutmeg, so 'stellar setter' reads as praise; read literally it is our star, the sun, that sets and briefly vanishes.
explanation.definitionFit: During an eclipse of the sun the Moon blocks its light, so our star temporarily disappears from view.

clue.text: Evergreen head girl

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
Meg is a girl's name, short for Margaret

explanation.surface: A tribute to an ever-youthful head girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Nutmeg was the Guardian pseudonym of Margaret Irvine, the setter this puzzle remembers; the girl's name MEG is her own.
explanation.definitionFit: The nutmeg is a tropical evergreen tree whose seed gives the familiar spice.

clue.text: Most disorderly disturbance stopped by Julie shedding clothes

indicators.note: something stopped by another has that other plugged into it, as a bottle by a cork

parts.note: unrest is public disturbance or agitation

indicators.note: taking off clothes strips the outer layer, so the outside letters of the name go

parts.note: the name with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A rowdy scene halted when Julie starts stripping.
explanation.walkthrough: Shedding clothes reads as Julie undressing; for a word it means losing its outermost letters at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruliest is the superlative of unruly, meaning the least orderly or controllable.

clue.text: Nice crossword compiler left local spot

parts.note: the compiler refers to herself as me, which in French (as spoken in Nice) is moi
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A pleasant setter walks out of a neighbourhood haunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city, not the adjective, so the setter's 'me' is French. 'Local' marks a dialect word: moil is a regional term for a stain or spot of dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: In dialect use moil means to soil or defile, and a moil is a smear or mark of dirt.

clue.text: Joy of genealogy regularly recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the kept letters are read back to front
regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: The pleasure of tracing family history, fondly remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is a feeling of great delight, so it is a synonym of joy.

clue.text: Material of singular kind, full of witticisms

indicators.note: a thing full of something else has that something packed inside it

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
puns are plays on words, a kind of witticism
ilk means type or kind

explanation.surface: A fabric of a unique sort, covered in jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: S and ILK join to make SILK, which then holds PUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun silk is yarn or fabric spun from short waste silk fibres, so it is a material.

clue.text: Irish climber in Scottish town

parts.note: Ir is an abbreviation for Irish
a vine is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: A mountaineer from Ireland arrives in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is a plant. Irvine was also the surname of Margaret, the setter remembered here.
explanation.definitionFit: Irvine is a coastal town in North Ayrshire in south-west Scotland.

clue.text: Actor to rhyme 'dissolute' and 'fruit'

indicators.note: dissolute means loose-living, so the letters are loosened and recombined

parts.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer is asked to find a rhyme for two awkward words.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks pretend 'dissolute' and 'fruit' are words to rhyme with; one is the anagram signal and the other the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry tomato is a small round tomato variety, and botanically a tomato is a fruit.

clue.text: Mum hearing about cunning of much-respected women

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the next

parts.note: a hearing in court is a trial
arch means slyly knowing or cunning

explanation.surface: A mother hears about the guile of venerated women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a sound signal; it is a court case. The definition is a phrase, 'of much-respected women', standing in for an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Matriarchal describes rule or authority held by mothers or senior women, the much-respected heads of families.

clue.text: Abrupt Russian gent forged autographs

indicators.note: abrupt means cut short, so the country's name loses its end
forged means hammered into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the word with its final letter cut off
taken as written

explanation.surface: A curt man from Russia faked some signatures.
explanation.walkthrough: Forged autographs fits the surface perfectly, but 'forged' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograph is a person's handwritten name, which is exactly what a signature is.

clue.text: Writing articulate solutions to clues for neophytes

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language

indicators.note: to articulate is to speak clearly, so the piece is given as it sounds

parts.note: in crosswords, the answers entered in the grid are called lights

explanation.surface: A guide to explaining crossword answers clearly for beginners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights' is crossword jargon for the answers written in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Proselytes are new converts to a faith or cause, so they are neophytes, beginners in it.

clue.text: Instrument making comeback in Bratislava

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the letters run in the opposite direction
in tells us the letters sit inside the place name

parts.note: letters two to six of the city's name

explanation.surface: A musical instrument returns to favour in Slovakia's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked plucked string instrument from the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Watertight evidence proceeded to trap one at the top

indicators.note: in a down answer, the top comes first, so this piece is placed above the other
to trap something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ran means went or proceeded
I is the Roman numeral one
proof is conclusive evidence

explanation.surface: Cast-iron evidence went on to catch the person at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watertight evidence' looks like one phrase; the definition stops at 'Watertight'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainproof item keeps rain out, so it is impervious to water, which is what watertight means.

clue.text: Chap in ladies' underwear worried rectories

indicators.note: worried means shaken or troubled, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man in women's lingerie alarmed the local vicarages.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a cross-dresser; the definition means a man working in the corsetry trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsetier is a man who makes or fits corsets, so he is in the business of ladies' foundation garments.

clue.text: Rude movie about tango and sex with variable capacity to inflame

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged word goes round the next piece
rude here means crude or roughly made, so the word's letters are left unrefined and jumbled

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns or variables

explanation.surface: An explicit film featuring a tango and sex has a mixed ability to arouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rude' reads as describing the film's content, but it only signals the rearrangement; 'it' for sex appeal is an old-fashioned euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotivity is the quality of stirring up strong feeling, so it is the power to inflame emotions.

clue.text: First of two educational establishments in African capital

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter of two
unis is short for universities

explanation.surface: The first of a pair of colleges opens in a North African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia in North Africa.

clue.text: Spoilt brat naughtily hiding ring at back of socket

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so the letters take in the next piece
naughtily suggests misbehaving, so the letters refuse to stay in their order

parts.note: ten letters to be rearranged
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A badly behaved child is concealing a ring in a hidden place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoilt' reads as the anagram signal but is part of the letters; 'naughtily' does the shuffling. The socket is the eye socket.
explanation.definitionFit: Postorbital is an anatomical term for what lies behind the orbit, the bony eye socket.

clue.text: Cod can initially upset stomachs

parts.note: can and bog are both slang for a toilet

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters of the following words count

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Fish that can quickly turn your stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cod' looks like the fish; here it is the adjective meaning fake. Can and bog are British slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod as an adjective means mock or sham, so it shares the sense of fake that bogus has.

clue.text: Kind of pudding so unloved in the past

indicators.note: unloved means without love, and love in tennis scoring is a zero-shaped letter, which is removed

parts.note: the word with its love dropped
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A type of dessert that people didn't care for long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is nil in tennis, so it stands for O; SO without O leaves S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch from palm pith, cooked with milk to make the traditional British sago pudding.

clue.text: 5's covering ground

parts.note: surface reading: the setter Nutmeg covering familiar territory
cryptic reading: the lacy aril around the nutmeg seed, which is dried and ground into a spice

explanation.surface: Nutmeg the setter going over well-trodden territory.
explanation.walkthrough: Covering ground sounds like travel; read as covering, ground, it is the nutmeg's outer membrane turned into powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Mace is the spice made from the red aril that wraps the nutmeg seed, usually sold dried and powdered.

clue.text: Surprise short leg, strapping female

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to amaze is to surprise; its final letter is cut
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: An unexpectedly short-legged, well-built woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the half of the field behind the batter's legs is the leg or on side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazons were a legendary race of women warriors, so the word now means a tall, powerful woman.

clue.text: Princess about to occupy most of Kent resort

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so this piece goes within the other
most of means not all, so the resort's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Margate is a seaside resort in Kent, a county in south-east England
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A royal is about to take up residence in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as one phrase but splits into piece and indicator. Princess Margaret was the late Queen's sister; Margaret was also Nutmeg's own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Margaret, sister of Elizabeth II, is the best-known princess of that name.

clue.text: Unique kind of switch conserving energy

indicators.note: to conserve is to keep safe inside, so the switch holds the next piece

parts.note: an on-off switch is a common kind of switch
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A special energy-saving switch.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is something made or happening only once, so it is unique.

clue.text: Bluff sibling starts to think story is made up

parts.note: to con is to bluff or deceive
sis is short for sister

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letters of the words that follow

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A brother or sister, starting to think, admits a tale is fabricated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is made up' looks like it means invented, the story's fate; it means composed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that consists of certain parts is composed of them, i.e. is made up of them.
